2027 Hyundai Elantra N Monochrome Heads to Canada While US Buyers Wait for Confirmation
7 photos
Photo: Hyundai / edited
Hyundai's Canadian subsidiary has recently confirmed an Elantra N for people who aren't big on contrasting trim. The Monochrome edition brings a more subdued exterior, along with Alcantara for the cabin, forged wheels, and some carbon-fiber exterior components for good measure. Prior to Canada, the special edition was detailed for Australia and the South Korean market.
The Monochrome could reach US dealers later, but all three announcements so far give us no decision to report on. Customers in Canada, meanwhile, can start thinking about which version of the special edition they want. The version question matters a lot because carbon-fiber goodies are optional.
By default, buyers get the black-themed aesthetic and Alcantara interior treatment. The upper version adds mirror caps and a rear spoiler in carbon fiber, which are pretty interesting additions when you remember that no suspension or powertrain changes are in store for this fellow. Monochrome revisits the regular sedan's exterior details, reducing the visual competition between the body and accents.
You can see the form without a separate color drawing an outline around the lower half of the car, and that is particularly different from trying to disguise the N as a rental-spec Elantra. Abyss Black Pearl makes the most literal interpretation, drawing the dark and body details together. Performance Blue offers the more interesting one, so Monochrome doesn't automatically mean black paint.
Hyundai and the N division describe the wheels as newly designed forged items, yet both failed to mention any weight savings. The safe conclusion is to view it as a new design that puts an emphasis on reducing unsprung mass over looks alone. The upper version's carbon-fiber parts add a different material and finish to the mirrors and rear spoiler, yet Hyundai has once again failed to mention any weight savings.
Photo: Hyundai Hopping inside, buyers are treated to a little more than Monochrome-specific Alcantara here and there. Black buttons on the Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel also need highlighting, with Alcantara further appearing on select interior components.
Over in Australia , the Elantra N Monochrome goes by the name i30 N Sedan Monochrome. The i30 moniker also designates the European model, where you get non-N versions of the i30 in hatchback, wagon, and fastback specifications. Just like the i20 N, the i30 N for Europe has been discontinued due to strict emission regulations.
The i30 N Sedan Monochrome will first go on sale in the latter part of October 2026 in South Korea as the Avante N Monochrome, with details for other markets to be published closer to the planned rollout dates. In South Korea, the newcomer will go on sale on October 29. Two days later, it will be displayed at the Hyundai N Festival at the Everland Speedway.
All versions can be had with either a six-speed manual or an eight-speed DCT of the wet-clutch variety. The metric output figures are 280 ps (276 hp) and 40.0 kgfm (392 Nm or 289 lb-ft), with peak torque offered at 2,100 through 4,700 revolutions per minute. When N Grin Shift mode is engaged, the DCT version temporarily reaches 290 ps (286 hp).
